title: Failed-Trial Discount on In-Home PAP Therapy Equipment Sales
content:
# Failed-Trial Discount on In-Home PAP Therapy Equipment Sales

**Discount schedule.** A failed coverage trial is discounted when a patient buys outright the PAP Therapy Equipment unit that stands in their home:

| More days since setup than the class's trial period | Qualifying nights the usage summary credits | Discount |
|---|---|---|
| yes | fewer than 40 | 15 percent |
| yes | 40 or more but fewer than 50 | 8 percent |
| yes | 50 or more but fewer than 63 | 4 percent |
| yes | 63 or more | none |
| no | any | none |

Otherwise there is no trial discount; a device record with no usage summary carries none.

**Where it is read.** The days since setup are calendar days from the setup date on the device record to today, the setup date itself not counted, compared with the class's coverage trial length in days. The qualifying nights are those credited on the usage summary download in the device's service history (the latest one, where there are several).

**How the percentage acts.** The discount is a percentage of the unit's price as it stands before percentage discounts. Where the sale carries more than one percentage discount, the percentages are first added into one total percentage, which reduces that price once, rounded half up to the cent; the percentages never act one after the other.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical, 90-day trial)

- 91 days since setup, 39 nights credited: 15 percent. 40 nights: 8 percent.
- 120 days since setup, 49 nights: 8 percent; 50 nights: 4 percent; 62 nights: 4 percent; 63 nights: none.
- 90 days since setup, 20 nights: none — the trial period has not yet passed.
